issues.main_description_html:
Description

Update the Apply API so the photographer's location comes from location the photographer inputs manually — not from EXIF GPS metadata and not from image metadata.

Context

In the Review Photographer modal (Location tab), the photographer's coordinates show 0.0000° N, 0.0000° E — i.e. a missing/default (0,0) location. The location must be captured from what the photographer enters during apply, and the Apply API should persist that input instead of storing 0,0.

Acceptance criteria

  • The Apply API accepts and persists the location the photographer inputs.
  • Location is not derived from EXIF GPS metadata or any image metadata.
  • Valid coordinates from the photographer's input are shown in the Review Photographer → Location tab.
  • Missing/invalid location input is handled gracefully (no invalid 0,0 stored / clear validation).

RESULT

Added required latitude and longitude fields (plus optional addressLine1, addressLine2) to the Apply Photographer API payload. Validation rejects out-of-range coords and the (0,0) default. On create, nearest city is resolved via GetNearestCity and all location data is persisted in a single DB insert.

issues.display_title: Issue #21: Fix Photographer Profile Link in Approval Email (Missing Photographer Path Segment)
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

The link in the email is missing the photographer in the URL.

The "your photographer profile is now live" email renders:

View and share your profile here: https://360photographers.org//jack-von-eberstein-sgud

The slug (jack-von-eberstein-sgud) is present, but the URL has a double slash // where the photographer path segment should be. The base URL is being concatenated directly with the slug and the /photographer (or equivalent) segment is missing/empty.

Expected

https://360photographers.org/photographer/jack-von-eberstein-sgud

(confirm the correct public profile path with the frontend)

Investigation note

The profile URL is not constructed in this backend repo — only the Plunk send helper helpers.SendEmail (src/helpers/email.go) exists here, and UpdatePhotographerStatus (src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerStatus.go) does not build or send this email. The malformed link is therefore coming from either:

  • the Plunk email template (base URL + {{slug}} joined without the photographer path segment), or
  • whatever service actually triggers/sends the approval email (likely gothru-dashboard).

First step for the assignee: locate where the profile URL string is assembled, then fix the path.

Acceptance criteria

  • The profile link in the approval email points to the correct public profile path (no double slash, includes the photographer path segment).
  • Verified with a real approval email to a test inbox — the link opens the photographer's live profile.
  • Fix applied at the source (template or sender), with the correct base path documented.

RESULT

Root cause: profileUrl built as %s/%s (base + slug) — missing /photographer segment.

Fixed in both email paths:

  • src/action/v1/photographers/notifyPhotographerUpdate.go:85 → fmt.Sprintf("%s/photographer/%s", ...)
  • src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerStatus.go:106 → fmt.Sprintf("%s/photographer/%s", ...)

issues.display_title: Issue #22: Photographer Detail: Expose Available Portfolios + Default Auto-Open Type (Hide Preview When None)
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

If the user only has a Google portfolio then that should be auto-open — I do not need to click on it to open it.

e.g. https://360photographers.org/photographer/jaap-lotstra · https://360photographers.org/photographer/alin-bugeag-iki6

On the photographer detail page, the portfolio preview should auto-open the first available portfolio following this priority order, and hide the preview entirely when the photographer has none:

  1. GoThru portfolio → if present, auto-open
  2. Google portfolio → if no GoThru
  3. Panorra → if no Google
  4. Matterport → if no Panorra
  5. none → hide the portfolio preview section

Note: the empty Location (, ) shown in the screenshot is a separate, already-tracked issue (#20) and is not part of this task.

Backend scope (Project: Photographer API GO)

Today the detail endpoint returns only portfolioUrl (the GoThru RSS link) and exposes nothing about which portfolio types a photographer actually has, so the frontend can't know what to auto-open without probing each type. This task adds that to the API so the auto-open/hide logic is driven by one response.

Grounded in the codebase (brainstorm/PROJECT_ANALYSIS.md — action/ layer, Redis-cached detail):

  • Portfolio type enum (src/controllers/v1/photographerPortfolio/getPhotographerPortfolioByType.go:43-48): panorra=1, matterport=2, gothru=3, google=4
  • Special GoThru-RSS portfolio: https://gothru.co/port/{rssKey} via GothruRSS.RssKey — counts as a GoThru portfolio.
  • Detail action to extend: src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go (currently returns portfolioUrl only, no portfolio-type presence info).

Acceptance criteria

  • Photographer detail response reports which portfolio types have content (e.g. counts or booleans for gothru, google, panorra, matterport); GoThru RSS counts as gothru.
  • Response includes a resolved defaultPortfolio (auto-open) = first non-empty type in priority order GoThru → Google → Panorra → Matterport.
  • When the photographer has no portfolio of any type, the response clearly signals "none" so the frontend hides the preview.
  • Cache invalidation respected (portfolio add/delete updates the detail response).
  • Frontend consumes this to auto-open the default portfolio without a click and to hide the preview when empty.
  • Verified against example photographers alin-bugeag-iki6 and jaap-lotstra.

RESULT

Added portfolioTypes (boolean map) and defaultPortfolio (string or null) to photographer detail response.

  • Queries portfolio table grouped by type for photographer
  • GoThru RSS (rss.RssKey != nil) counts as gothru
  • Priority: gothru → google → panorra → matterport → null
  • Both fields cached with the rest of the detail response; existing cache invalidation covers portfolio add/delete
